title: 4. URINARY TRACK INJURIES DURING LAPROSCOPY AND THEIR PREVENTION.

4. URINARY TRACK INJURIES DURING LAPROSCOPY AND THEIR PREVENTION.

Most common major complication.

91 times higher litigation with these injuries.

Urinary bladder:

0.02 – 8.3%.

Comonest site = midline above Inter/uretric bar.

LAVH most common cause of bladder injury.

Damage can occur while:

Suprapubic port.

Separation of bladder from cervix

Prevention:

Aoid suprapubic port insertion (higer failure => rupture in space of retizius surgical emphysema.

Cystosubflation

CO2

Saline.

To identify margins of bladder in difficult surgeries but deflate before central & lateral seperation to avoid damage.

Adequate dissection of bladder from vaginal apex when cuff is sutured vaginaly and sepation done abdominally.

Angulation

Stenting.

Thermal

Extensive + deep => excision + re-anastomosis + re-implantation.

Transection

Upper 1/3 => ureterostomy/ end to end anastomosis with stenting.

Middle => uretro ureterostomy or trans uretro ureterostomy end to side anastomosis.

Trans => is not a 1st choice as it cuts the healthy ureter.

Lower => uretro neocyctostomy.

Tension free anastomosis is required, if not tension free due to short length of ureter, then go for Boari Flap or psoas hitch.

Psoas hitch:

Bladder is mobilized and fixed with iliopsoas muscle tendon to fill the gape.

Boari flap:

Upto 12 – 15 cm length can be added
